versions.runtimeLabel: TeaVM 0.13.1 (frozen release; its WASI backend was removed in 0.14.0). NOT the JVM: not comparable to the matrix Scala cells
versions.frontEnd: Scala 3.6.2 dotc (scala3-library_3 3.6.2 + scala-library 2.13.15 on the TeaVM classpath)

transforms: none on the sources; the same class files (one front-end compile per benchmark) feed both TeaVM backends
asymmetries: primary: the native column is TeaVM's C backend + LLVM clang -O2; the wasm column is TeaVM's own wasm emitter (no LLVM, no binaryen pass) + Cranelift, so the ratio mixes backend quality with the wasm cost

TeaVM runtime and GC differ per backend: the C backend uses its C runtime (memory.c, glibc) and the wasi backend its own Java-written/wasm runtime with linear memory sized by --min-heap/--max-heap; same heap flags on both
the wasm backend runs without wasm exception-handling instructions (--wasm-use-exceptions not set); the C backend uses its own mechanism
front end is Scala 3.6.2 (dotty.tools.dotc.Main), not the matrix build line, and TeaVM replaces the JDK class library with its own classlib: no HotSpot, no JIT, no JVM GC anywhere
TeaVM 0.13.1 output is not byte-reproducible: two builds of the same Dockerfile gave identical tak.wasm but a different bigint.wasm of the same size (cause not investigated)

na.fannkuch: TeaVM 0.13.1 cannot build it with either backend: 'ERROR: Method java.lang.Class.initializeImpl()V is native but has no org.teavm.interop.Import annotation on it' (reached via Array.tabulate -> ClassTag.apply -> scala.runtime.ClassValueCompat.<clinit> -> Class.initialize); fixing it needs a source or library change

v8SessionDrift.finding: dijkstra on V8 moves with how the process is launched (2026-10-27: 65,550,712; eight measurements on 2026-10-29: 65,251,892 to 65,407,630 instructions; ratio 1.871 to 1.879 over all nine) while identical invocations agree to within about 1,700 instructions; changing the driver's file name, its text or the container launch moves it by 34,000 to 149,000; the module imports no random_get, wasmtime reproduces to 194 instructions, a fixed clock_time_get changes nothing
v8SessionDrift.cause: the timing of V8's young-generation scavenges: with a 64 MB young generation (--min-semi-space-size=64) every variant (with and without the random_get override, two file names, two launch shapes) gives 65,296,144 to 65,297,064 instructions; the exact 2026-10-27 value was not reproduced (the pre-fix driver file is not kept); the published cell keeps the flags every V8 cell uses
